utterances.text: The accused is reading too fast. There is no English translation on the screen. We cannot interpret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without showing the English version, it's very difficult for interpreters to follow. So -- but we may collapse the English one for the benefit of the witness. Please read very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the only thing I can control, reading slowly. The rest is out of my hands. Let me repeat: "In the village of Novoseoci south of Sokolac, some 5 or 6 kilometres away from Sokolac, the weapons and lethal assets were handed over by the Muslim population to the representatives of the 2nd Romanija Brigade. The hand-over was carried out pursuant to an agreement and it is considered that the surrender was not complete, i.e., that not all the weapons were surrendered. On the 27th of July the military reported that not everything was handed over. How does that tally with what you knew as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have the document on the screen. I know that very little was handed over, that both sides laughed. The surrender was just ridiculous. I don't know how much was surrendered, but it was very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just a while ago we saw a reply by the president of the Municipal Assembly. Let us look at 65 ter 5377. Did you know what my position was with regard to the protection of the population of Muslim ethnicity which was not engaged in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have that text in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't need it. What did you know? Leave aside the text. Did you know anything about my position in this regard?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I was aware of your position because I was listening to you at a meeting at the municipality of Sokolac which I attended. You invited people to live together. You said that one ethnicity could not be expelled from an area, that Muslims should be provided all the staples for a normal life, that they should be protected on the ground, and to allow them to work and live freely. You especially emphasised and underlined the Geneva Conventions, and I believe that you spoke very well at that meeting and that you said exactly what should be honoured in the war in order to avoid any possible problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at -- look at 65 ter 5377.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We saw that the previous document was a reply to a telegram of mine. Please cast a glance at this document which will appear sometime soon on the screen for you to see. Can you read the document? It is in the Latinic script. The Trial Chamber can do it as well. Were you aware of this position of mine? Were you aware of such telegrams that I dispatched? How does this tally with what you knew about my position?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have it in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is in harping. It says here --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: "All the villages" --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "... in which the Muslim population under" -- I don't see the word in between.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: "... surrender weapons and do not intend to fight against us must enjoy the full protection of our Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. President of the municipalities will be responsible for this."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How does this tally with what you knew about my position with regard to minorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The document is self-explanatory. It says here that those people must be protected on the ground and that they are protect on the ground, that they enjoy protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have no objection. I just note that the contents are virtually duplicative of D95. It's not in exactly the same form in the sense that this is the individual telegram, whereas the other document repeats the contents of the telegram. It says that it's been sent to the following municipalities. So I'm not sure it's necessary to have this in evidence, but I don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we see D95.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. It is a group of telegrams. This was sent to Sokolac. There were others that were sent to other municipalities. It is 65 ter 01109, and there is also a D number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure that she got the 65 ter number correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This text is the same but this telegram is proof that it was delivered to Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive that separately, i.e., 65 ter 5377.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, you said and you confirmed that before the 21st of July there was no fighting. How did things develop? Was the peace preserved? Was there fighting? If there was fighting did it subside or did it intensify?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of August, as I've already told you, the villages that didn't want to surrender weapons were approached by the 2nd Romanija Brigade in order to disarm them. However, they opened fire on the 2nd Romanija Brigade, and since their numbers were smaller they had to withdraw from the villages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to look at 1D4391, dated 19 September, three days before the developments in Novoseoci. 1D4391.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander Krstic reported on the 19th of September, and says: "Due to frequent provocations and attacks on our positions in Serbia [as interpreted] population by Muslim extremists, we wish --" and I will stop here. Were there any civilian Serb casualties at the hand of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. In Cvrcici village they killed three people. Jovan Sekulic was killed in a particularly heinous way. They skinned him. They inserted a rod in his penis and left him alive, and the -- that was a terrible state. And then Saffron Krsmanovic was killed. He was driving in his village. He was shot at. Saffron was killed, his son Milenko was injured, and the tractor was pierced with bullets. Peric who escaped from the shooting went missing and his whereabouts are not known. His remains have never been found, but he's not among the living. In the village of Dzimrije, which is not in our municipality, another man was killed. In the village of Ozarkovici, another man was killed. In all the borders areas there were casualties. In Gornje Babine Milomir Batinic was shot at but he managed to escape to Sokolac. This is proof that there were casualties there, including the seven people who were taken to Zenica, to the prison there. In other words, there were a lot of dead around our municipality in the suburbs. Since all the Serbs were engaged in the army that they joined the 2nd Romanija and the 216th, the Serbian village were empty and the Muslims in the neighbouring villages were armed. They were at a distance of 5 to 10 minutes. They arrived from Zepa and from elsewhere. So those villages were reinforced by men, and they had sent their women and children to Sarajevo. Imagine a village where there are women and children and another village where there are only armed men. How could the Serbs sleep calmly? It's -- the way it transpires is that they were not left alone but -- by us but it was just the other way round.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you said empty Serb villages, what did you have in mind, what kind of emptiness?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the lack of people who were able to fight, the lack of men fit for combat and resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now it says here: [As read] "We inform you that on the 20th and 21st of September, 1992, we are going to carry out active operation towards the villages of Kuti and Micivode with the aim of liberating the Serb villages from the Muslim extremists." Does this imply that they are going to be liberated from ordinary civilians or extremists?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: From extremists, because everybody who had weapons were extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So without reading the remaining part of this document, can it be admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3191, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that on the 21st and the 22nd, the 2nd Romanija Brigade incurred losses? Were there any burials in Sokolac on the 22nd?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of July you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: September.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: There were funerals, but I don't remember whose it was. If you would give me a name I might remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 20 you mention some soldiers who lost their lives.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: That was in the village of Kaljina. I tried to speak about that a while ago but we skipped it. They were returning from the front line, from their positions. The Muslims were deep in our territory in the village of Kaljina or there about, and they planted mines there that killed four or five men amongst whom was Nenad Tabakovic. So four or five soldiers were killed on that occasion which was immediately before the incident in Novoseoci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 1D4390, please. I believe that the Prosecution might have a better number that conceals a translation as well. Could the other participants have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So 20th of September that -- 22nd of September, that is the day when the incident in Novoseoci took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see an English translation for this. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation is going to appear. We'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you can see that this is a combat report by the 2nd Romanija Brigade. Can we look at the bottom of the page. 65 ter 24854 is identically the same with the exception of paragraph D which reads: [As read] "During the previous night and day, the brigade suffered losses from the 4th Motorised Battalion. Two soldiers whose names we do not know were killed, and those were Bogdan Borovcanin and Darko Krsmanovic."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic wait until the interpretation is completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can't find document in that number but yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think that -- it's not identical, but I think the same -- essentially the same contents are in the 22nd of September report that's in evidence as P5438. It seems to be in a different format but I think this information is in that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In this document paragraph D was supplemented by providing the names of the victims from the 2nd Romanija Brigade. It seems that what I read was not recorded, so it can perhaps be admitted into evidence if -- I'm going to continue: "... Bogdan Borovcanin, Darko Krsmanovic, and Nenad Tabakovic. One member of the 1st Motorised Battalion was injured." Now, can we have this document -- well, we didn't hear Mr. Obradovic's response.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is correct that these three were killed and that one was injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I understand that this document is already in evidence as P5438.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Excellency, except that in this version paragraph D is shorter, but wait a minute. As I see it, it seems there is something there after all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we show Mr. Karadzic the second page. D -- I think I was able to follow everything you read out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Now I see that they are identical. Thank you. There is another version without the names, and then we had a Serbian version with the names. So since this is in evidence, we're not going to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, do you know exactly on which date these men from Novoseoci were killed? In what way and who did this, which unit? And who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there is the date somewhere. You are confusing me a bit. I have trouble following you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me help you. The Prosecutor asked you if you received formal information about that. You said that it was informal. On page 67, you were asked the following: It was common knowledge what happened in Novoseoci, and you said yes. When you said that, did you mean that everybody knew that or did you know that as an official?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I knew that in my official capacity, but stories were circulating around Sokolac regarding the killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know any details? Were these people shot dead and what were the circumstances under the killings took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 30, you speak about the fact that some villages put up resistance and that fighting developed there.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, look what this document says. It speaks about operations, active operations, from infantry weapons and mortars. "During last day and night, the enemy attacked our forces along several axes in the sector of defence of our forces, and these operations are carried out with the use of antitank mines, mortars, and other weapons." How does this correspond with the knowledge that you have about fighting taking place there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that there was fighting in the area, and I heard that they had antitank shells, that they had mortars, that the village of Meljine was engaged in combat with the 2nd Romanija Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph on page 64 in Exhibit P3296, you -- it was put to you that Mr. Macar said that plans had been drawn up for disarming individuals in possession of illegal weapons way back in May. Does that mean that these plans were immediately implemented?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they were not implemented until the fighting started. When the 2nd Romanija Brigade started and wanted to disarm the people, that's when the fighting broke out because they resisted these attempts. If there had not about any resistance there would not have been any fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us -- you said that there was in the border areas, these Muslims who attacked Serb civilians, where did they all come from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, those were mostly people from the villages on the edges of the municipality, the village of Kaljina, Ivazovici [phoen], Gornja Selo, Sasevci [phoen], and Meljine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you rule out the possibility that these attacks were carried out by people from Novoseoci, and did you have any information about the groups that raided the area from Olovo and other places?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: According to Krstic's report, there were 7.000 armed men in Olovo. There were 30 to 40 in Kaljina, and in Knezina and other Muslim villages, there were approximately 30 to 40 armed men respectively, and he said that the attack came from Golovo through these villages in order to create confusion in the Serbian Army and enable them to link up with Zepa, then Visegrad, and Ilivaca, and eventually to capture the whole area and link it up with Pale and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please look at 1D4389. Can we please zoom in and can the other participants be provided with a translation in display.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a combat report dated the 23rd of September, which is one day after the Novoseoci incident. In the second paragraph, it says that the enemy's trying to constantly infiltrate sabotage group lay mines on supply roads and therefore create confusion and cut off supply channels in the sector of Karacic, Olovske Luke. There were several soldiers who were wounded and the attack was repelled, et cetera. What do you know about the activities of these groups and was this sabotage and terrorist activity something that endangered the civilians and the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: There were several incidents that landmines were planted on a number of roads because after these several killings the army placed the roads under their control. All of this had an adverse effect on the Serbian people, causing them to be frightened and posting guards around their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the next page. Let's look at item C. It reads: "In villages that have been recently mopped up, Kuti, Micivode, and Novoseoci, there are still straggling groups which escaped, which is why some units are searching the area and discovering and destroying these groups as well as controlling roads and important routes." Further down it says that someone was buried in Sokolac and so on and so forth. What did you know about the arming of these groups? Were they armed, and did they also lay mines deep inside our territory?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I know that a group was detected in the area of Kustravica in late 1993. They were moving through villages across Mount Devetak going as far as the Drina almost. Another route they used was across Kopito hill, also deep inside our territory. There was a group of people who were in contact with Zepa, so such groups constantly moved through the wooded area such as Devetak, Kustravica, and further afield to Olovo and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As a policeman, please tell us: When you received such reports, would you be able to find elements to launch an investigation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: An investigation against whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there indications here that there were some unlawful killings?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Of course there were unlawful killings. You wait for someone in his own territory, you lay mines, and people get killed. Of course investigations were supposed to be launched if it was known who did it, but the army was in no position to find that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: Based on this report, would you have initiated an investigation against the 2nd Romanija Brigade? Does it contain certain elements of unlawful behaviour?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why I would launch a report when the Muslims were doing worse on their side than these people were on ours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, did you have enough? How many policemen did you have? Did you have enough police forces to go about your duties, and did your policemen join the forces at the front line or were they all at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: We did not have enough forces even to carry out purely political -- police tasks. There were cases of breakthrough through the lines when police were used to patch up at such locations, so the police did take part in combat. They would go for five or six days and there would be a rotation of another group -- with another group. So we never had enough men, especially not trained men who could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at 1D7974. This is from the Executive Board of Sokolac municipality. The date is 24th of September, two days following Sokolac. The second item it says there is a unanimous conclusion that there are no bases for the implementation of legal and other regulation. In paragraph 4 it states: [As read] "The public security station is in no position to prevent looting, smuggling, and armed attacks on civilians. Not even the introduction of the curfew did provide any visible results. The functioning of the authorities is put into question as well as the implementation of laws, municipal regulation, as well as conclusions and orders of the Presidency of RS." It goes on to say the lack of will or power -- well, what was it that the security station lacked?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: We lacked power, force. We didn't have enough people, and even the ones we did have were not adequately trained. Just a moment ago I was trying to say that the chief of station was a writer, an emotional person who thought that things would stop when he had a conversation with criminals. I would bring them in to the station. He would talk to them and release them instead of allowing me to detain them and submit criminal reports. That is why those criminals felt even stronger. After that this Bilic, I don't know whether he was removed or he resigned himself, but things were put in order at the station later and it functioned pretty well throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Karadzic, how does it arise from the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was this question whether there were no investigations against the army and they did not seem to have enough manpower to investigate criminals. So this brings about the issue of the ability of the police station to do something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the witness raised the issue of lack of personnel with regard to the investigation of the military personnel. Given the time, why don't you conclude? How many more minutes do you need, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two, perhaps three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were shown Mr. Tupajic's answer to me when he said that he had no forces to protect the Muslims. Despite that, did you try to cover up any suffering on the part of Muslims or did you also undertake investigations when the victims were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: There was no covering up. Everything was known that would take place during any given day because people talked, so there was no covering up on either of the sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we briefly look at 65 ter 19810.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you personally take part in investigations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Me? Sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 65 ter -- yes. Are you familiar with this document? There is a translation, because I have it in my hand.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the 20th of July, an on-site investigation, and this is a record of it, it involves Judge Gavrilovic and Carkic and so on. The injured party is Salih Dautovic and so on. Who is Salih? What was his ethnicity? Where was he from, and what did you do as part of that investigation? How many of them were there? How many of you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer, yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This incident is already discussed in the witness's statement as well as the document related to this investigation. I didn't touch it in my cross-examination, so it just doesn't arise. It was already addressed in direct. If Mr. Karadzic wanted to ask additional questions about it, he should have done that at the outset. It don't arise from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, because of the admission of Mr. Tupajic's letter, this shows in fact how the local authorities are continuing to try to protect the Muslims, and I think that that opened the door to this to come in.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And just for your reference, it's at paragraph 21 where he discusses this incident and the investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is seven days --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber agrees with Mr. Robinson's observation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us who were the perpetrators and what happened with this Mr. Dautovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dautovic was a forest ranger in Tocionik. He worked there. He was a fine man. His village a few days was -- before that been deserted. The people left themselves, and I talked to him, asking him why they left. He told me, "Dragan, I don't know." He told me that they went to Olovo and that he refused so that I could come the next day -- he would come the next day after he had said good-bye to the inhabitants of Sokolovac. We sat down at Krunic's place and I told him if need be just give me a ring at any time of day or night, there's no problem, if there are any disturbances of law and order, if there's anyone touching you or doing anything criminal. We said our good-byes and I left. I told him if you're interested, give it a thought, because I could take you to Olovo to take you to your people. On Monday morning people from Grbici, some young guys awaited me and told me that Salih Dautovic and his family and another two people were killed in their own home. We set up an on-site investigation team including representatives of the [indiscernible] state security, the crime police, an investigating judge. We went to the location, saw what happened, submitted a criminal report, and it was against an unknown perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is under number 4?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Obradovic, station commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the full name would be Dragomir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No, just to say no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Please, when these were for an exchange taken to Kula, did they have the status of prisoner there or did they await an exchange?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: They awaited an exchange. I don't know how many days later it took place and they went to Sarajevo. Some people called me and thanked me for it, for how they were transported and saying that no one mistreated them and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. Thank you for being a good policeman and thank you for having testified today.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go. The hearing is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I considered it to be my duty to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of March, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.57 p.m.,
